items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: So I took the horn, while we were playing Bunny Berigan, Herman Autrey, Bessie Smith... Bunny and I -- and oh, it was beautiful!

ctx.x: This is on a Sunday, and it wasn't open. The door opened, and we went in, there was nobody in there then, but shortly two or three people started coming in, a few people. You know, I look up and Bunny Berigan walked in, and I saw a couple of pieces of horns laying around there, they're Bunny's horns. Bunny was working there. Fats sat at the piano and started bling bling bling linga, playing and playing. Bunny came in and sat there, so Bessie Smith walked in soon, and people started coming in.

Before you knew what was happening -- he never explained nothing, what is happening. The session was on. So he said, "Come on!" I said, "I ain't got no horn." Bunny say, "Here, use one of mine." So I took the horn, while we were playing Bunny Berigan, Herman Autrey, Bessie Smith. So Fats would take four or five. Bunny would take four or five. Herman would take four or five. That's the way until the place was packed, they was standing on top of each other.
